title: Deployment capacity radar + hotfix standup
content:
Attendees: Sofia Chen (chair), Marcus Trent, Aisha Kapoor, Diego Vasquez, Priya Nair, Chen Li (observability), Emma Shore (SRE)

Date: 2026-03-12 09:30 PT
Meeting context: Weekly release engineering cadence focused on capacity planning for the next two release trains, prioritization of the hotfix queue, and verification of recent canary behavior after the v2026-03-10 deploy.

Agenda:
- Quick status on active release trains (alpha / bravo)
- Hotfix queue triage and ownership
- Capacity radar: GPU pool headroom, burst policy, and cross-region routing
- Canary review: latency/error changes, rollback thresholds
- Runbook gaps and ownership for H-117/H-118
- Action items and next checkpoint

Summary / highlights:
- Alpha train (scheduled deploy window 2026-03-15): on track. Major items are model spinups for bert-2x quantized, and two infra PRs that change autoscaler thresholds (infra#1843). We flagged potential tail latency regressions at seq_len=2048; observability will run focused traces this afternoon.
- Bravo train (scheduled deploy window 2026-03-18): currently light on user-facing changes; contains routing policy tweaks for cheaper variants. We recommended a canary sash for the price-based routing change to avoid simultaneous exposure across regions.
- Hotfix backlog has 5 tickets. Two are high priority (H-117: tokenization edge case causing 500s for certain user inputs; H-118: KV cache eviction bug causing memory growth). H-117 has a fix candidate in staging; H-118 needs a small patch and regression test under long-lived streams.
- Capacity radar: GPU pooled capacity at 73% baseline utilization; headroom is ~27% including reserved burst. East US1 has the tightest headroom (18%). We proposed temporary burst reallocation from West EU to East US1 for the next 72 hours to cover predicted alpha train ramp.
- Canary review for v2026-03-10: overall token-level latency +3.6% median, p95 increased from 210ms to 240ms on weight-shared models. Error rate bump observed for 3rd-party tokenizer failures (0.12% -> 0.6%). No cascading SLO breaches, but we opened post-deploy tasks to harden tokenizer retries.

Detailed notes:
1) Release trains
- Alpha: owners Sofia (release lead), Marcus (infra), Aisha (model onboarding). Blockers: infra#1843 (autoscaler tuning) pending review; model quantization baseline test failing on GPU type A100-80GB for long prompt sequences. Decision: keep alpha canary at 10% traffic for first 30m then 30% for next 2h, contingent on p95 staying <300ms.
- Bravo: owners Priya (release lead), Diego (routing). Contains policy change: fallback to gpt-lite-quant for non-critical tiers when latency > SLO. Decision: use progressive sash (1%->5%->20%) separated by 45m monitoring windows.

2) Hotfix triage
- H-117 (JIRA RE-1721): Tokenizer boundary mismatch. Repro in staging with the legacy tokenizer plugin. Fix in branch token-fix/RE-1721, PR ready. QA to run fuzz suite. Owner: Aisha. Target: ship in emergency window 2026-03-13 03:00 PT if fuzz passes.
- H-118 (JIRA RE-1728): KV cache eviction bug with long-lived streamed sessions. Memory growth seen on dedicated pools after ~36 hours. Mitigation: increase eviction aggressiveness + short-term restart policy for affected nodes. Owner: Marcus. Need longer regression test in dedicated env. Target: hotpatch by 2026-03-14.
- H-119 (lower priority): telemetry label mismatch on per-route metrics. Won't block releases.

3) Capacity radar and routing
- Observability snapshot (Chen Li): baseline GPU utilization 73%; autoscaler buffer as currently configured allows 12% surge. Expected alpha train bump ~10% sustained within peak hours. East US1 projected to drop below safe headroom if multiple canaries roll simultaneously.
- Temporary action: manual reassign 2 nodes from West EU reserved pool to East US1 for 72h. Diego to coordinate with cloud infra team to avoid interrupting dedicated tenant contracts. If reassign impossible, enable cross-region fallback and increase canary ramp delays.
- Long term: proposal to add regional reserve buckets to the autoscaler config (RFC draft due 2026-04-02).

4) Canary and post-deploy observations
- v2026-03-10 canary metrics flagged p99 tail spikes on sequence lengths >1024. Root cause trace points to kernel selection fallback when quantized kernels mismatch expected layout. Action: add kernel selection telemetry and a guard in runtime to prefer older stable kernel for seq_len > 1024 until we ship dedicated kernel fix.
- Tokenizer errors: correlated with a third-party dependency update on 2026-03-09. Short-term mitigation: pin tokenizer to 2.1.7 for hosted clusters and add retry loop in the tokenizer adapter. Aisha to own rollback plan + communication.

5) Runbooks / docs
- Runbook gap: H-118 has no documented safe rollback for long-lived streams; action: Marcus to author stream-eviction-runbook.md and attach to RE-1728 by 2026-03-13 EOD.
- Emergency contact updates: Emma to verify on-call rotations include infra-on-call handoff notes for weekend deploys.

Action items (owners and dates):
- Aisha: merge token-fix/RE-1721 after fuzz pass; push hotpatch if green. Target: 2026-03-13 06:00 PT. Linked: JIRA RE-1721, PR token-fix/RE-1721.
- Marcus: implement temporary eviction aggressiveness and run long-lived stream regression for H-118. Provide runbook draft. Target: 2026-03-14.
- Diego: coordinate cross-region node reassign request with cloud infra and provide go/no-go by 2026-03-12 17:00 PT.
- Chen Li: run sequenced trace job for seq_len distribution and upload kernel-selection logs to observability. Target: 2026-03-12 19:00 PT.
- Priya: prepare canary sash plan (phases and rollback criteria) for bravo train and share in the release channel. Target: 2026-03-13 12:00 PT.
- Emma: validate on-call contact list and weekend deploy handover. Target: 2026-03-13 EOD.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: simultaneous canaries in East US1 could push region into <10% headroom. Mitigation: stagger canary windows, enable cross-region fallback, or temporarily increase burst capacity.
- Risk: hotpatch H-118 causing service interruptions if eviction overly aggressive. Mitigation: staged rollout to dedicated pools first; monitor memory and error budgets closely.
- Risk: tokenizer rollback might impact feature parity for some customers. Mitigation: communicate rollback window and expected behavior to CS; keep a feature-flagged path for new tokenizer.

Notes / loose questions to follow up:
- Confirm whether reserved dedicated tenant SLAs permit temporary node reassign for short-term capacity balancing. (Diego follow-up with customer success/legal)
- Add a lightweight regression harness for long-lived streams to CI so we catch H-118 earlier. (Marcus + SRE)

Meeting adjourned: 10:10 PT
Next checkpoint: Quick hotfix sync 2026-03-13 08:00 PT for H-117/H-118 status. Full release engineering weekly on 2026-03-19 at regular time.

Appendix: quick change log for recent deployments
- v2026-03-10: runtime kernel selector update (opt-in), tokenizer third-party pinned to 2.1.8 (temporary), packer autoscaler tuning (infra#1830)
- Hotpatch H-116 (2026-03-11): immediate fix for streaming heartbeat timeout (rolled to 8 clusters)

Free-form notes / scribbles:
- Consider adding an "allocation reserve" flag per release train so we can pre-lock minimal capacity from pool rather than reassign post-facto.
- Investigate p95 delta after quantization; might need a micro-benchmark harness for 2048 seq_len patterns.
- If H-117 shows non-deterministic fuzz failures, set up CI fuzz on the fast-path tokenizer adapter only.
